BOOMS HAVE BEEN PLACED IN THE CREEK TO TRY TO CONTAIN THE SPILL. A BYSTANDER IN THE AREA OF THE INCIDENT WAS INJURED. THE PERSON WAS TAKEN TO A HOSPITAL WITH UNKNOWN INJURIES.

BOOMS HAVE BEEN PLACED IN THE CREEK TO TRY TO CONTAIN THE SPILL. A BYSTANDER IN THE AREA OF THE INCIDENT WAS INJURED. THE PERSON WAS TAKEN TO A HOSPITAL WITH UNKNOWN INJURIES.

Skytruth Analysis

Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON AUGUST 22, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708).

Lat/Long: 48.420639, -123.397599 (Approximated from street_address)
Report DescriptionDESCRIPTION OF SPILL SITE AND SURROUNDING AREA: THERE WAS AN OVERFLOW OF WASTER THROUGH THE BYPASS ON THE 6TH, 7TH AND 8TH OF NOV. THERE WAS EXCESS RAIN ON THE 6TH. ON THE 7TH AND 8TH GATES WERE LOWERED WHICH RELEASED EXCESS SEWAGE THROUGH THE USUAL WATERWAYS. DESCRIPTION OF SPILL SOURCE, CIRCUMSTANCES, CAUSE AND ADVERSE EFFECTS OF THE SPILL: AN OVERFLOW WAS CAUSED WHILE THE MAIN PROCESSOR FOR THE PLANT WAS BEING REPLACED OVER THREE DAYS. A SMALL AMOUNT OF SEWAGE WAS NOT CONTROLLED DURING MAINTENANCE. THE PROCESSOR WAS REPLACED WITH A HIGHER CAPACITY PROCESSOR. DURING THE REPLACEMENT THERE WAS AN OVER RELEASE. THE PLAN WAS TO LOWER GATES AS A SAFETY MEASURE AS IT WAS THOUGHT LESS RISKY THAN SHUTTING THE PLANT DOWN FOR MAINTENANCE.
